elements.element: Customer owns all Deliverables created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Section 14.2 states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause addresses capitalized “Deliverables” only. Without a supplied definition showing that Deliverables include all work product, ownership of work product is not established.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Vendor expressly and irrevocably assigns all right, title, and interest in each Deliverable upon creation.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all right, title, and interest in all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment covers each Deliverable but does not expressly cover all work product, and no definition equating the two is supplied.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing IP.
elements.evidence: The clause says Vendor retains “Vendor Technology” under Section 14.3, but neither that definition nor Section 14.3 is supplied, so coverage of all pre-existing IP cannot be verified.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to any Vendor IP embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No embedded-IP licence appears in the rendered clause. The margin comment’s reference to Section 13.2 is non-operative, and Section 13.2 was not supplied.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no embedded-IP licence or perpetual duration.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is irrevocable, but no irrevocable embedded-IP licence is granted.

elements.element: The embedded Vendor IP licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no royalty-free embedded-IP licence.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed.

elements.element: No joint ownership arises.
elements.evidence: Exclusive Customer ownership precludes joint ownership of Deliverables, but the clause does not address joint ownership of broader work product, Customer Data, or other relevant IP.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: Vendor retains “Vendor Technology,” but the supplied language does not establish that this term includes generic tools.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: Know-how is not mentioned, and the meaning of “Vendor Technology” cannot be verified from the supplied clause.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause assigns ownership of Deliverables to Customer rather than granting the fallback licence.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is perpetual.
elements.evidence: No Deliverables licence or perpetual licence duration is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is irrevocable, but the fallback requires an irrevocable licence, which is absent.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is worldwide.
elements.evidence: No worldwide licence is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free licence is stated.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer ownership ordinarily carries use rights, but the required fallback licence and its express use permission are absent.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No licence expressly permitting modification is granted.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: No sublicensing right is granted.

elements.element: The Deliverables licence permits Customer to exercise the licensed rights for its business.
elements.evidence: No licence or business-use scope is stated.

result.reason: The redline clearly flips ownership of Deliverables and includes an effective present assignment, but it does not independently address all work product, embedded Vendor IP licensing, Customer Data, or the full no-joint-ownership requirement. The fallback licence is also absent. References asserted only in the non-operative margin comment, or to sections not supplied, cannot cure these omissions.
